item.title: Security
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
AdCanvas connects to the accounts that run your business, so we treat security as part of the product.

Your account

  • Two-step verification with an authenticator app, plus recovery codes.
  • Sign in with Google.
  • Sessions are stored as hashed tokens and can be signed out from Settings.
  • Roles (owner, admin, member, viewer) and an audit log of sensitive actions.

Your data

  • Credentials for connected platforms are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM.
  • All traffic is served over HTTPS with strict security headers.
  • Protection against cross-site request forgery and server-side request forgery.
  • Rate limits on sign-in and AI requests.
  • Export or delete your workspace data at any time — see Data deletion.

Connected ad platforms

AdCanvas only creates paused drafts in Google Ads and Meta. Nothing spends money until someone on your team enables it in the ad platform. Disconnecting an integration deletes its stored credentials.

Reporting a vulnerability

Email [SECURITY EMAIL]. We acknowledge reports within [X] business days and don't take legal action against good-faith research.

item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Effective date: [EFFECTIVE DATE]

This policy applies to everyone who uses AdCanvas. If you break it, we may suspend or terminate your access under the Terms of Service.

You may not use the Service to:

Create unlawful or deceptive advertising

  • Make false, misleading or unsubstantiated claims, including health, financial, earnings or "get rich quick" claims.
  • Use fake reviews or testimonials, or endorsements without the disclosures required by law (such as the FTC Endorsement Guides).
  • Run discriminatory targeting or exclusions in housing, employment, credit or other protected categories, or get around platform rules for special ad categories.
  • Promote illegal products or services, or advertise regulated products (such as alcohol, gambling, cannabis, pharmaceuticals or financial products) without the required licenses and compliance with platform and legal rules.
  • Impersonate a person, brand or organization, or create content meant to mislead people about its origin.

Misuse personal data or messaging

  • Upload special-category or sensitive personal data (health, biometric, precise location, children's data, government IDs, financial account numbers) or customer lists, unless the Service expressly supports it.
  • Send email or SMS without the consent and opt-out mechanisms required by law (such as CAN-SPAM, TCPA, GDPR/PECR or CASL), or buy, sell or scrape contact lists in violation of law or platform terms.
  • Track or profile individuals in violation of privacy law.

Abuse the Service or connected platforms

  • Break platform terms of the ad networks and tools you connect, including getting around their review, rate limits or policies.
  • Probe, scan or test vulnerabilities, or bypass security, authentication or usage limits, without written permission.
  • Reverse engineer the Service, or use it to build a competing product.
  • Upload malware, or interfere with the Service or other users.
  • Resell the Service, or share accounts, except as your plan allows.

Misuse AI features

  • Generate content that is illegal, hateful, harassing, sexually explicit involving minors, or violates others' intellectual property.
  • Try to extract our prompts or models, or use outputs in violation of our AI provider's usage policies.

item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Template notice: This DPA reflects GDPR Article 28 and common US state-law service-provider terms. Have counsel review it, attach the EU Standard Contractual Clauses and UK Addendum where you transfer data internationally, and replace every [BRACKETED] placeholder.

This Data Processing Agreement ("DPA") forms part of the Terms of Service between [COMPANY LEGAL NAME] ("Processor") and the Customer ("Controller").

1. Definitions

"Personal Data", "Processing", "Data Subject", "Personal Data Breach" and "Supervisory Authority" have the meanings given in the GDPR. "Data Protection Laws" means the GDPR, the UK GDPR, the Swiss FADP, the CCPA/CPRA and other applicable privacy laws.

2. Details of processing (Annex I)

3. Processor obligations

Processor will:

  1. Process Personal Data only on Controller's documented instructions (these Terms and Controller's use of the Service), unless the law requires otherwise, in which case Processor will inform Controller where legally permitted.
  2. Make sure that personnel authorized to process Personal Data are bound by confidentiality.
  3. Implement the technical and organizational measures in Annex II.
  4. Assist Controller with data subject requests, security, breach notifications, data protection impact assessments and prior consultations, taking into account the nature of the processing.
  5. Notify Controller without undue delay, and in any event within [48] hours, after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting Controller's data, with the information reasonably needed to meet Controller's obligations.
  6. Make available the information necessary to demonstrate compliance, and allow audits. Audits will be satisfied first by Processor's then-current third-party certifications or reports, and otherwise will take place no more than once a year on [30] days' notice, at Controller's cost.

4. Subprocessors

Controller gives general authorization for the subprocessors listed at /legal/subprocessors. Processor will give at least [30] days' notice of new subprocessors, and Controller may object on reasonable data protection grounds. Processor imposes data protection terms on each subprocessor that are no less protective than this DPA, and remains responsible for their performance.

Integrations that Controller enables (for example Slack, ad platforms or CRMs) are Controller-directed recipients, not Processor's subprocessors.

5. International transfers

Where Personal Data is transferred from the EEA, the UK or Switzerland to a country without an adequacy decision, the parties incorporate the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module 2, and Module 3 where applicable), the UK International Data Transfer Addendum, and any Swiss amendments, as further described in [ANNEX III].

6. CCPA/CPRA service-provider terms

Processor will not sell or share Personal Data. It will not retain, use or disclose Personal Data outside the direct business relationship or for any purpose other than performing the Service, and will not combine it with other data except as the CCPA permits. Processor will comply with the CCPA and notify Controller if it can no longer meet its obligations.

7. Deletion and return

When the Service ends, and at Controller's choice, Processor will return or delete Personal Data within [30] days. Backups will be deleted within [35] days, unless the law requires storage. In-app export and deletion tools are available at any time.

Annex II — Technical and organizational measures

  • Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest. Integration credentials are additionally encrypted with AES-256-GCM at the application level; passwords are hashed with scrypt.
  • Role-based access control (owner/admin/member/viewer), least privilege, multi-factor authentication for our administrative access, and an audit log of security-relevant actions.
  • Logical separation of customer workspaces.
  • Unguessable share-link tokens that the owner can revoke.
  • Vulnerability management, dependency patching, and [annual] penetration testing.
  • Backups with tested restore, and a documented incident response plan.
  • Vendor due diligence for subprocessors.
  • Employee confidentiality agreements and security training.

item.title: Data Deletion Instructions
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
You can delete your data from AdCanvas at any time. This page is also the data deletion URL we give to platforms such as Meta and Google.

Delete data yourself (immediate)

  1. Open AdCanvas, then open the board menu (the grid icon next to the campaign name).
  2. Choose Privacy & data → Delete everything. This permanently deletes all boards, comments and AI assets, and disconnects every integration, which deletes the stored access tokens.

To remove only one platform connection, select that integration on the canvas and click Disconnect. Its stored credentials are deleted right away.

Revoke access from the platform side

You can also remove AdCanvas's access in each platform's settings:

  • Meta (Facebook/Instagram): Settings & privacy → Settings → Business integrations → AdCanvas → Remove.
  • Google: myaccount.google.com/permissions → AdCanvas → Remove access.
  • LinkedIn, TikTok, HubSpot, Shopify and others: remove the app from the connected-apps settings in that platform.

When access is revoked, we stop syncing data, and the stored credentials stop working. Delete your data in AdCanvas as described above to remove previously synced metrics.

Ask us to delete it

Email [PRIVACY EMAIL] from your account email address with the subject "Data deletion request". We will confirm within [5] business days and complete deletion within [30] days. Backups roll off within [35] days. We may keep limited records where the law requires it, such as invoices.

You can check the status of a request by replying to our confirmation email.

item.title: How to map a full-funnel ad campaign before you spend a dollar
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Most campaigns fail quietly. Not because the ads were bad, but because nobody wrote down how a click was supposed to become a customer. Mapping the funnel first fixes that.

1. Start from the outcome

Write down the one number that matters — purchases, demos booked, trials started — and what it's worth to you. Everything on the map should lead there.

2. Add the traffic sources

List every channel that will send people in: paid social, search, display, email, partners. For each one, note the budget and the expected cost per click. This is where most of your spend sits, so be honest about the numbers.

3. Draw the path

Connect each source to where it lands — a product page, a landing page, a lead form — and on to the next step. Ask at every step: what happens to the people who don't convert here? That's where retargeting and follow-up emails belong.

4. Put a conversion rate on every arrow

You won't know the real numbers yet. Use benchmarks, then multiply through: 10,000 visitors × 3% to lead × 20% to customer = 60 customers. If the result doesn't pay for the budget, you've learned that for free.

5. Replace guesses with data

Once the campaign is live, connect your ad and analytics accounts so real numbers replace the forecast, step by step. The weakest step is usually obvious within a week.

Tip: In AdCanvas, AI Build does steps 2–4 from a one-paragraph brief, and the forecast updates as you change anything on the canvas.

item.title: Writing ad copy that fits every platform’s limits
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Every platform truncates differently. Copy that reads well on Meta gets cut mid-word on Google. Here are the limits worth memorizing, and how to write within them.

The limits that matter

Limits change; check each platform's current specs before you launch.

Write the long version first

Start with the full message — who it's for, the outcome, and the proof. Then cut it down for each placement. It's much easier to shorten a clear idea than to stretch a slogan.

Make every headline stand alone

Google mixes headlines in any order, so each one has to make sense by itself. Give each a different job: the benefit, the offer, the proof, the call to action.

Match the step in the funnel

Cold audiences need the problem and the promise. Retargeting audiences already know you — give them the proof and a reason to act now.

Tip: AdCanvas writes ad packs for each step and flags anything over a platform's limit before you export or publish it as a paused draft.
item.excerpt:encoded: Headlines, descriptions and primary text for Google, Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok — with the limits that matter.

item.title: Budget pacing: catch overspend before month end
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
A monthly budget that's spent by the 20th isn't a budget. Pacing tells you early whether you're on track, so you can adjust while it still matters.

The basic check

Divide spend to date by the share of the month that has passed. If you've spent $6,000 of a $10,000 budget on day 15 of 30, you're pacing at 120% — on track to spend $12,000.

Why it drifts

  • Auction changes. Competitors raise bids, especially near holidays.
  • Learning phases. New campaigns often spend unevenly in the first days.
  • Broad targeting. Automated campaigns expand to find volume.

What to do about it

  1. Check pacing by channel, not just in total — one channel usually explains the gap.
  2. Look at cost per result alongside spend. Overspending at a good CPA can be an opportunity, not a problem.
  3. Adjust daily budgets in small steps (10–20%) to avoid resetting learning.

Automate the alert

Nobody remembers to check every day. Set an alert for when pacing passes a threshold, say 110%, and review then.

Tip: The AdCanvas dashboard shows budget pacing against your plan, and scheduled alerts can post to Slack when a channel drifts.
item.excerpt:encoded: A simple daily check that keeps campaigns on plan, and what to do when they drift.
